title: Plugin guidelines (ChatGPT plugins): commerce, prohibited goods and checkout
notes: Read through the .md variant at 2026-11-15T02:59Z UTC (2026-11-14 local). Commerce section: plugins may conduct commerce only for physical goods. Checkout section: plugins should use external checkout on the developer's own domain; Instant Checkout, in beta, is available only to select marketplace partners and may expand; until then external checkout is required and no other third-party checkout may be embedded in plugin UI; the section links OpenAI's agentic commerce docs at /commerce, which no longer describe Instant Checkout. The prohibited goods list covers adult content and sexual services, gambling, illegal or regulated drugs, drug paraphernalia, prescription and age-restricted medications, illicit goods, malware and surveillance, tobacco and nicotine, and weapons and harmful materials; it does not list alcohol.

title: Add UI to your MCP server (ChatGPT plugins): components, extensions and checkout in the plugin UI
notes: Read through the .md variant at 2026-11-15T03:00Z UTC (2026-11-14 local) by the refresh's verifier. Plugin UI components run inside an iframe in ChatGPT and talk to the host through the MCP Apps bridge. The ChatGPT extensions list includes Instant Checkout with window.openai.requestCheckout. The section on the ChatGPT payment sheet says embedded checkout with the sheet is in private beta for select marketplaces; the component calls requestCheckout after the user chooses to pay, and ChatGPT sends the selected payment token to the MCP server's complete_checkout tool.

title: Authentication (ChatGPT plugins): OAuth 2.1 under the MCP authorization spec, client identification and mutual TLS
notes: Read through the .md variant at 2026-11-15T02:47Z UTC. Authenticated MCP servers implement OAuth 2.1 conforming to the MCP authorization specification, linked at revision 2025-11-25; the authorization response validation rules are linked at revision 2026-07-28. ChatGPT prefers Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), also supports dynamic client registration and predefined clients, uses PKCE with S256 and RFC 9207 issuer identification. ChatGPT presents an OpenAI-managed client certificate for mutual TLS (leaf SAN dnsName mtls.prod.connectors.openai.com, chaining to the OpenAI Connectors mTLS intermediate CA); servers can also allowlist ChatGPT's published egress IP ranges. ChatGPT does not support machine-to-machine OAuth grants or customer-provided client certificates.

title: ChatGPT HTTP message signatures key directory
notes: Read at 2026-11-15T02:49Z UTC: HTTP 200, content type application/http-message-signatures-directory+json, cache-control no-store. One Ed25519 key (kty OKP) with nbf 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z and an exp seven days after the read, plus the members signature_agent (https://chatgpt.com) and purpose (ai). The response itself carries an RFC 9421 signature with the tag http-message-signatures-directory. Keys carry a rolling expiry, so the key id is not reproduced as a stable value.

title: RFC 7239: Forwarded HTTP Extension
notes: Read as text at 2026-11-15T02:56Z UTC. Section 5.5: extension parameters SHOULD be registered in the HTTP Forwarded Parameter registry. Section 8.1: the Forwarded header cannot be relied upon to be correct, because any node on the way to the server, including the client, may modify it.

title: American Express Publishes Intent Intelligence Framework for Trusted Agentic Commerce
notes: Read at 2026-11-15T04:45Z UTC (HTTP 200). The Create Intent API captures the customer's purchase instructions and constraints, such as merchant and maximum budget; the customer authenticates and signs off on the intent; an Intent ID and a Proof of Intent Token are created; the token can be used to obtain a payment credential, scoped to the authorized intent, that the agent uses at checkout instead of the card number. The framework is available through the ACE Developer Kit. American Express says it is engaging with EMVCo and supporting the x402 Foundation's work.

title: Intent Intelligence: Building Trust in Agentic Commerce
notes: Read at 2026-11-15T04:45Z UTC. By Inderpreet Hundal and Gianna Rotondo. Intent sign-off by passkey, or delegated by the issuer to a third party such as the agent or a wallet provider. The Proof of Intent Token is a JSON Web Token that expires on the date the user confirmed and can be single-use or multi-use. Data elements: Purchase Summary, Max Amount, Intent Expiry, Merchant Data, Item-Level Conditions, Maximum Number of Transactions, Order Context (Intent or Cart) and Purchase Criteria.
